new_statements.translation: p.20: '... the accent falls on the first syllable of the word when the vowel is short; the unaccented consonant in internal or final position is realised either as a fricative or as lax. The same accentuation is found in words ...' p.96: '... [the prefix carries the] accent when the radical vowel is short; the radical carries the accent when the vowel that follows it [the prefix] is long; it [the prefix] has an indefinite value when not followed by a determiner. The radical and the prefix are bound together ...'

Differences from the report's quote are only Google's spaces before punctuation and one full stop the…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent is word-initial (on the class prefix / first syllable) when the radical vowel is short, but falls on the radical (second) syllable when that syllable has a long vowel; i.e. a quantity-sensitive choice within the first two syllables, default initial. Yashina 2011's four stress-marked transcriptions (['gərusə] vs [bʊ'la:gɔ], [mʊ'lɔ:sɔ:ɾ], [ʊ'ɟa:ɔ:ɾʊlɔ]) pattern exactly this way.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing seen in the accessible fragments.
new_statements.exceptions: Snippet p.25 ties accent to consonant articulatory force with a demarcative function and mentions differentiation 'pour les villages' (possible local variation); p.19 states a full study of accent was not undertaken. The orthography guide (Svetlichnaia 2013 §8.1) notes Mandinka loans behave exceptionally, but with respect to the ATR diacritic, not stress. Full context of pp.19-25 not seen.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent ('première syllabe du mot'); p.96 concerns prefixed nouns (prefix vs radical). Tendeng treats accent together with consonant fortis/lenis realisation as demarcative. Only snippet context available, so whether p.20 describes Gusiilay proper or a comparison lect cannot be fully verified.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources examined describe Gusiilaay as spoken in Thionck-Essyl (Tionk Essil), Bignona dept., Casamance = Glottolog gusi1246 / ISO gsl. Note that Glottolog's reference list for gusi1246 also carries Sagna's and Bassène's works on Gújjolaay Eegimaa / Jóola Banjal, which is a different (though closest-related) lect, ISO bqj (Glottolog Bandial, band1340); those were not used. Tendeng 2007 p.25 snippet hints at accentual differentiation between villages/quarters, so the rule may be stated for a particular local variety; unverifiable without the full pages.

sources.note: No stress-placement rule and no prosody section (contents: vowels/ATR harmony, consonants, morphophonology). Only §1.4 'Vowel loss' (p.17; PDF p.18) gives stress-marked forms ['gərsə]~['gərusə] 'an evening', [b'la:gɔ]~[bʊ'la:gɔ] 'a way', [m'lɔ:sɔ:ɾ]~[mʊ'lɔ:sɔ:ɾ] 'myrrh', [ʊ'ɟa:ɔ:ɾlɔ]~[ʊ'ɟa:ɔ:ɾʊlɔ] 'you have walked', and states 'As the examples show the vowels loss happens in the syllables which are not stressed'. The marks fall on the prefix when the root vowel is short (gə-rusə) and on the root syllable when its vowel is long (bʊ-la:gɔ, mʊ-lɔ:sɔ:ɾ, ʊ-ɟa:ɔ:ɾ-), consistent with the Tendeng sni…

sources.note: The written 'accent' (acute á é í ó ú) marks +ATR ('lourd') vowels, not stress; §8.1 p.15 'Tous les mots qui prennent l'accent sur la dernière syllabe, souvent d'origine mandinka, vont être écrits sans l'accent' (efalo 'âne' prononcé efaló) concerns where the ATR diacritic would fall, not word stress.
